name: Sharpen and maintain kitchen knives
blurb: Beyond a one-off sharpening: knowing when to hone, when to sharpen, how to store and how to wash so a good knife lasts thirty years.
gear: A magnetic strip or knife block
steps: Learn the difference between honing (realigning the edge, weekly) and sharpening (removing metal, every few months).
Learn to hone properly: consistent angle, light pressure, alternating sides, a few strokes only.
Learn whetstone sharpening: raise a burr on one side, then the other, then refine and strop.
Learn the destroyers: the dishwasher, glass or stone boards, leaving knives wet, and scraping the board with the edge instead of the spine.
Store on a magnetic strip or in a block, never loose in a drawer.
Set a maintenance rhythm and stick to it — a schedule beats waiting until it is unusable.
tips: Scraping chopped food off the board with the blade edge dulls it faster than cutting does. Use the spine.
Hand wash and dry immediately, even for stainless.
proof: Every knife in your kitchen passes the paper test and you can say when each was last sharpened.
